question: A 6-year-old boy presents to his pediatrician accompanied by his mother for evaluation of a rash. The rash appeared a little over a week ago, and since that time the boy has felt tired. He is less interested in playing outside, preferring to remain indoors because his knees and stomach hurt. His past medical history is significant for an upper respiratory infection that resolved uneventfully without treatment 2 weeks ago. Temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 115/70 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, and respirations are 18/min. Physical exam shows scattered maroon macules and papules on the lower extremities. The abdomen is diffusely tender to palpation. There is no cervical lymphadenopathy or conjunctival injection. Which of the following will most likely be found in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "6-year-old boy with rash and abdominal pain" -> "possible systemic condition" -> "consider vasculitis" -> "leukocytoclastic vasculitis is a type of small vessel vasculitis" -> "associated with skin rashes and abdominal pain" -> "high likelihood given symptoms" -> 85%

CHAIN: "6-year-old boy with maroon macules and papules" -> "suggests possible vasculitis" -> "abdominal tenderness indicates systemic involvement" -> "leukocytoclastic vasculitis can cause these symptoms" -> "other options less likely based on presentation" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Recent upper respiratory infection" -> "can trigger autoimmune responses" -> "increased risk for conditions like vasculitis" -> "leukocytoclastic vasculitis fits clinical picture" -> "other options do not correlate with symptoms" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Tiredness and joint pain in a child" -> "suggests possible inflammatory process" -> "leukocytoclastic vasculitis can present this way" -> "maroon macules indicate skin involvement" -> "high probability of finding leukocytoclastic vasculitis" -> 90%
analysis: The clinical presentation of the 6-year-old boy, including the rash, abdominal pain, and fatigue, suggests a possible diagnosis of Henoch-Schönlein purpura (HSP), which is a form of small vessel vasculitis. The maroon macules and papules on the lower extremities, along with abdominal pain, are characteristic of this condition. In HSP, leukocytoclastic vasculitis is commonly found on skin biopsy, indicating the presence of small vessel inflammation. Therefore, leukocytoclastic vasculitis is the most likely finding in this patient.
